text:
eli: Heads-up — I'm drafting a Terraform change to provision a GPU nodepool with reserved on-demand capacity + a larger spot pool as fallback. Want a quick sanity check before I open the PR.

maya: Which cloud? and paste the TF + k8s snippets when you have them.

eli: AWS. Plan is: a small on-demand nodegroup for stable inference (2 nodes g4dn.xlarge), and a separate spot nodegroup with mixed instance types and higher max. Draft TF: ```resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu_reserved" { instance_types = ["g4dn.xlarge"] desired_capacity = 2 capacity_type = "ON_DEMAND" tags = { role = "gpu-reserved" } } resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu_spot" { instance_types = ["g4dn.xlarge", "g5.xlarge"] desired_capacity = 0 capacity_type = "SPOT" max_size = 20 tags = { role = "gpu-spot" } } ``` Also plan to taint spot nodes with `gpu=spot:NoSchedule` and label `nodepool=gpu-spot`.

sam: Quick notes: 1) Make sure spot nodegroup has `capacity_rebalance`/`instance_interruption_behavior` knobs where supported. 2) Deploy a spot interrupt handler (we already run one in infra). 3) For GPU jobs that need checkpoints, add an annotation so they get drained gracefully.

rachel: We have node-termination-handler but current cordon/drain timing is short. For GPUs we should extend to ~2m to allow model checkpointing. Also check PDBs — if PDB blocks eviction, pods will linger and waste the node. Consider `maxUnavailable` for stateful workloads.

eli: Agreed. Proposed k8s pod change (for checkpointable jobs): ```apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: annotations: checkpoint: "true" labels: workload: "training" spec: tolerations: - key: "gpu" operator: "Equal" value: "spot" effect: "NoSchedule" terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120 ``` We'll also add a small controller that watches for the interrupt handler label `spot-interrupt=true` and triggers an annotated drain workflow for pods with `checkpoint=true`.

maya: For TF — double-check whether EKS node group supports EC2 Capacity Reservations directly. If not, we might need to create an `aws_ec2_capacity_reservation` resource and pin instance types/azs. That said, CR is expensive; maybe reserved on-demand is enough for critical inference (finance approval needed).

sam: FWIW we previously decided to avoid CR because of cost/ops complexity. If the on-demand nodegroup has `desired=2` and we tag it, it's fine for now. For spot, make sure autoscaler has `--balance-similar-node-groups` and `--ok-total-unready-count` tuned for shorter termination windows.

infra-bot: deployed-checker: Terraform plan for PR/infra/gpu-nodepools shows +2 aws_eks_node_group.gpu_reserved, +1 aws_eks_node_group.gpu_spot (changes include instance_types and tags). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1245

eli: I'll open PR with: TF changes, k8s manifests for interrupt-handler config + small operator, and a README section for runbook (how to respond to preemptions). Requesting review from @maya and @rachel. Also need someone to run `tf apply` in staging and sanity-check scaling/eviction behavior.

maya: I can apply to staging tomorrow at 09:30 PT. Please add `apply:staging` label to the PR and a short checklist (smoke tests, node labeling, drain simulation).

rachel: I'll review the k8s manifests. Two asks: 1) emit Datadog metrics for `spot_preemptions` with tags `nodepool:gpu-spot, instance_type` and 2) add nodegroup tag `lifecycle=spot` for billing queries.

sam: Also add a simple e2e: deploy a tiny GPU job with `checkpoint=true`, then simulate spot interrupt and ensure pod drains and checkpoint is uploaded within the TTF window.

eli: Great — thanks. I'll draft the PR and ping everyone once it's up.

(threads like this will be short — followups in the PR for specifics)
